chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim and others, via different chains, transmitted it in raised form, saying:

The Quraysh demolished the Ka'ba because floodwaters would come from the upper areas of Makkah and enter it, causing it to crack; and a golden gazelle with legs of jewels was stolen from the Ka'ba, and its walls were short — and that was thirty years before the Sending of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So the Quraysh intended to demolish the Ka'ba, rebuild it, and expand its floor area. Then they became fearful and worried that if they put the pickaxes to it, a punishment might descend upon them.

So Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said: 'Leave me to begin — if it pleases God, nothing will befall me; and if it is otherwise, we shall stop.' So he climbed upon the Ka'ba and moved a stone from it, and a snake appeared before him, and the sun was eclipsed. When they saw that, they wept and supplicated, saying: 'O God! We intend nothing but repair!' So the snake disappeared from them, and they demolished it and moved its stones around it until they reached the foundations that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had laid.

When they wanted to expand its floor area and moved the foundations that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had laid, an intense earthquake struck them along with darkness. So they refrained from it. The building of Ibrahim was: length thirty cubits, width twenty-two cubits, and height nine cubits. So the Quraysh said: 'We should increase its height.' So they built it. When the construction reached the place of the Black Stone, the Quraysh quarrelled over placing it, and every tribe said: 'We have the greatest right to it — we shall place it.'

When the dispute intensified among them, they agreed to accept the judgment of whoever entered through the gate of Banu Shayba. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) appeared, and they said: 'This is Al-Amin (the trustworthy one) who has come!' So they made him the judge, and he spread his cloak — some say it was a Tarauni garment that he had — and placed the Stone in it. Then he said: 'Let a man come from each quarter of Quraysh.' They were: 'Utba ibn Rabi'a from Banu 'Abd Shams, Al-Aswad ibn Al-Muttalib from Banu Asad ibn 'Abd Al-'Uzza, Abu Hudhayfa ibn Al-Mughira from Banu Makhzum, and Qays ibn 'Adiyy from Banu Sahm. They lifted it, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) placed it in its position.

found what was suitable for the Ka'ba — wood, decorations, and other things. They purchased it and brought it to Makkah. The measurement of that wood matched the construction, except for the Hijr. When they finished building it, they clothed it with Al-Wasa'id, which are the cloaks.

key_terms.الأمين: Al-Amin — 'The Trustworthy One', an epithet of the Prophet Muhammad before his mission
key_terms.الحجر الأسود: The Black Stone — a sacred stone embedded in the eastern corner of the Ka'ba
key_terms.القواعد: The foundations — specifically the original foundations laid by Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham)
key_terms.الكعبة: The Ka'ba — the cubic structure at the center of the Grand Mosque in Makkah, considered the holiest site in Islam
key_terms.الوصائد: Al-Wasa'id — cloaks/fabrics used to clothe the Ka'ba
key_terms.الوليد بن المغيرة: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira — a prominent Qurayshi leader who volunteered to begin the demolition

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the Quraysh rebuilding the Ka'ba and how did the Prophet Muhammad resolve the dispute over the Black Stone?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the historical account of the Quraysh demolishing and rebuilding the Ka'ba approximately thirty years before the Prophet's mission. It records the divine signs that appeared when al-Walid ibn al-Mughira dared to begin demolition — a snake and a solar eclipse — which frightened the Quraysh into repentance. Most significantly, it records the Prophet Muhammad's wise resolution of the tribal dispute over placing the Black Stone, earning him the title al-Amin (the trustworthy), by having representatives from each of the four quarters of Quraysh collectively place the stone using his cloak.
